s0101.literal: Above they did not emulate the worthy, below they did not deliberate on merit; yet right and wrong were mixed together, and [all], by rule, received fiefs.
s0101.idiomatic: Those at court did not look to exemplars for how to behave, nor did merit matter in discussion at lower levels—but right and wrong were jumbled anyway, while everyone routinely took their share of enfeoffment.

s0102.literal: It resembles expediency for the moment and is no lasting system; should it thereafter go unchanged forever, such [a policy] belongs to those occasions of nuisance and clutter, too: it is likewise the doorstep to gradual chaos.
s0102.idiomatic: It looks like stopgap pragmatism, not enduring institutions. If nothing is ever corrected, restless officials will seize on every inconsistency, and disorder will creep in by degrees.

s0103.literal: As for the rise of states, [it arose] because the Nine Clans dwelt together in intimacy and harmony, and common folk were harmonious and cooperative.
s0103.idiomatic: States flourish when imperial kin knit close ties and ordinary people pull together.

s0104.literal: As for its decline: [the fault lay] when bone and flesh [kin] drifted estranged apart, and the hundred surnames [the people] harbored departed hearts.
s0104.idiomatic: States rot when flesh-and-blood kin grow cold and estranged and the populace loses heart altogether.

s0105.literal: Therefore Xia's domain was restless, and Yi Yin withdrew to Yin [Shang];
s0105.idiomatic: So when Xia could not govern its own realm, Yi Yin withdrew to Shang territory.

s0106.literal: Yin's domain lacked harmony, and the Lüs entered Zhou.
s0106.idiomatic: When Shang fractured, ministers of the Lü line crossed over into Zhou.

s0107.literal: Shang looked to Xia's posteriors as mirror; departing matters' caution is truly the mirror of coming affairs.
s0107.idiomatic: Shang drew its moral from Xia's aftermath: what has already ended is genuinely the precedent for what comes next.

s0109.literal: Formerly during the Shu campaign they levied troops and mounts from Liang province, strong Qiang and Hu boys, promising them lavish reward; upwards of five thousand men followed Deng Ai to strike rebels, yet their feats all ranked foremost.
s0109.idiomatic: When Shu was overrun, recruits from Liangzhou—Qiang horsemen, Hu recruits—were summoned with extravagant promises of pay. More than five thousand accompanied Deng Ai, and each company earned top marks.

s0110.literal: Yet the 'Yihai' imperial edict: commander-governors in commanderies and prefectures were treated differently from inner and outer [central] armies; though [some] attained highest merit ranks, none qualified for investment [as lord].
s0110.idiomatic: But the decree of Yihai set provincial generals apart from armies under the metropolitan command—even first-class feats did not merit a feudal patent.

s0111.literal: Only the Soldiery led by Governor of Jincheng Yang Xin, by reason of the pressure they applied at the Jiangyou approach, had thirty men who received enfeoffment.
s0111.idiomatic: Only the detachment of Jincheng governor Yang Xin, which pressed the Jiangyou corridor, saw thirty men actually ennobled.

s0112.literal: West of Jincheng, those not in Xin's section: not a single man was enfeoffed.
s0112.idiomatic: West of Jincheng, outside Xin's command, nobody was given a title at all.

s0113.literal: If [they] fell under central-army precedent, though [only] lower merit [rank], they would necessarily [be made] marquises;
s0113.idiomatic: Had the same men been tallied as central-army troops, even middling performance would have won them a marquisate.

s0114.literal: if [instead they served] amid province and prefecture, though merit was lofty [they went] uninvest—this misses what they call 'those near withhold no double bounty' and 'those distant leave no grace unspent.'
s0114.idiomatic: Caught in the provincial tally, lofty deeds went unrewarded—which contradicts the principle that insiders should not be spared honors twice while outsiders go empty-handed.

s0115.literal: Your subject has heard fish hang [on the line] owing to sweet bait, and reckless men die for rich reward.
s0115.idiomatic: Sweet bait hangs the fish; big pay draws brave men willing to gamble their necks.

s0116.literal: Hence Jing Ke admired Crown Prince Dan of Yan's sense of righteousness; Zhuan Zhu responded to King Helü of Wu's favor; dagger-hand brandished in Qin courtyard, Wu blade glinted in fish belly—they viewed death like returning homeward—is it not rooted in motive!
s0116.idiomatic: So Jing Ke answered Prince Dan's call, Zhuan Zhu repaid King Helü's esteem—one waved a dagger in the Qin court, the other drew a blade from a salted fish—and both met death as calmly as going home. Such deeds always have their reasons.

s0117.literal: As for meritorious name and hefty reward—is what shi [gentlemen-officials] race for—unfairness arousing resentment has had a long pedigree.
s0117.idiomatic: Glory and gold are what officers chase; jealousy over uneven reward is as old as government itself.

s0118.literal: The 'Odes' declares: '[The cuckoo-dove] Shijiu is in the mulberry; its chicks are seven.'
s0118.idiomatic: The Book of Songs reads: 'The turtle-dove rests in the mulberry; it nurtures seven chicks beneath its wings.'

s0119.literal: The good man—the noble man—his demeanor stands one [the same];
s0119.idiomatic: The virtuous man's bearing is steadfast and even.

s0120.literal: ' Your subject holds that persons of such kind ought likewise to receive lordly rank patent.
s0120.idiomatic: Your servant submits that men of this stature deserve feudal patents as well.'

s0121.literal: Zhuo's serial memorials beforehand and afterward invariably met imperial review.
s0121.idiomatic: Each time Zhuo spoke up earlier or later at court, his words reached the emperor's desk.

s0122.literal: Yet his person petty, his offices lacking kin backup, advancement and seniority unseen, thereby he seized extended leave to return hometown.
s0122.idiomatic: But he lacked rank, lacked a patronage circle, saw no promotions, so he took indefinite leave for his home district.

s0123.literal: On quitting, he dispatched his heir to ascend a memorial stating:
s0123.idiomatic: Before leaving he sent his son up with another memorial that read,

s0124.literal: Your servant has received favor three successive reigns, split tally guarding frontiers—trial-duty without achievement, submerged unadvancing several years—the strength of humble dog horses [this subject] has none left to devote.
s0124.idiomatic: I have borne three sovereigns' favor, wielded tally on the marches yet produced no deeds, sunk in office for seasons without rise—whatever strength a petty retainer retains is spent.

s0125.literal: Your Majesty magnifies broad-ranging hearing, adopts wild men's words—pardons [me] infringing office-boundaries' crime, asks not after defiant remonstrance's offence—Heaven-earth's bounty runs deep; toward your servant indeed it suffices.
s0125.idiomatic: Your Majesty listens widely and weighs even a crank's counsel—forgiving my overstep of jurisdiction and never punishing my blunt defiance. Heaven and earth could heap no greater kindness on me.

s0126.literal: Your servant hears that one's loyal servant to his sovereign is akin to one's filial son to his parents—advancing yields glad joyous celebration—not coveting salary;
s0126.idiomatic: A faithful minister resembles a dutiful child: advancing to office sparks honest joy—not greed for place.

s0127.literal: retreating then bears melancholy grieving—not cherishing stipend;
s0127.idiomatic: Leaving office brings mourning faces—not clinginess to paychecks.

s0128.literal: that intent settles in forgetting not illuminating sovereign-parent's glory—they are circumstances passion cannot constrain itself.
s0128.idiomatic: The point is only to brighten ruler and forbears—to stop would betray every feeling altogether.

s0129.literal: Your servant prostrate meditates mourning, harboring inward utmost regret-grievances: bred in wild borderlands yet long stationed outer commands; since returning I hold illness, never attended audience—your Majesty still knows not who your servant is: this grievance-number-one of servant.
s0129.idiomatic: I mourn inwardly: raised beyond the pale yet always sent to distant posts—recalled only to fall ill, never summoned to court—so Your Majesty still does not know who I am. That is my first regret.

s0130.literal: [I] encountered an age of turning fortune, seized an era of crises, yet could not suspend fame-merit atop bamboo slips and silk—that regret-number-two.
s0130.idiomatic: I lived stirring times yet never carved deeds into the historians' slips—that is sorrow two.

s0131.literal: Attending unto sage-luminous ruler, yet haggard shrunken lame-wasted—uttering strength yet unable—ought return death beneath earth—that regret-three.
s0131.idiomatic: I serve a luminous throne while my body wastes—wish to exert myself yet cannot—weighs as if buried already—that is sorrow three.

s0132.literal: Lamenting two parents decayed early vanished, brethren together withered off—Filial Reverence obtains no farther stage at household-portal—that regret-four.
s0132.idiomatic: Father and mother left early and brothers vanished too—nowhere remains to practise filial devotion—that is sorrow four.

s0133.literal: Summer daylight suddenly has passed—winter night's turn again arrives—man's life century length still esteemed insufficient—but your servant mid-years bound disaster—that regret-five.
s0133.idiomatic: Summer afternoons vanish overnight; winters return swiftly; a century still feels brief—yet midway I am blasted by affliction—that is sorrow five.

s0134.literal: Ashamed beneath sun-month's nourishment, shamed confronting vast azure without repaying—this servant's rationale holding five regrets sighing mournful, confronting homeward-road self-mournful.
s0134.idiomatic: I blush under sun and moon, shame myself before Heaven with nothing to repay—five resentments haunt me sighing toward the journey home.

s0135.literal: Speech has proverb stating: '[Showy] embellished speech is empty; ultimate speech is solid; bitter speech is medicine; sweet speech is illness.'
s0135.idiomatic: The old saw runs: 'Flattery is hollow, depth is real, bitter counsel is physic, honeyed words are poison.'

s0136.literal: ' Your servant wishes speak All-under-Heaven Great Peace, yet spirit-tortoise divine fox not appeared, transcendence-mushroom magic-reed not born, qilin not roamed spirit-birds' park, phoenix not displayed form at Grand Ultimate courtyard—this servant's basis for not daring florid speech and becoming sycophant.
s0136.idiomatic: I would love to announce universal peace, but no tortoise omens, no lucky fungi, no qilin stalking the royal menagerie, no phoenix wheeling the inner court—so I cannot mouth pretty lies and play the flatterer.'

s0137.literal: Formerly Han Gaozu first settled All-under-Heaven; at that time garrison-soldier Lou Jing ascended memorial remonstrating: 'Your Majesty taking the empire does not match Cheng-Zhou's way, yet wishes compare numinous-sublimity with Cheng-Zhou's completion—your servant privately holds [the two] unequal.'
s0137.idiomatic: When Gaozu had just pacified the realm, the conscript Lou Jing warned: 'You seized the realm differently from the Zhou founders, yet you want to match their spiritual perfection—I see no parity.'

s0138.literal: ' Thereupon Han's Ancestor sensed insight, deeply ingested his words, bestowed him surname Liu.
s0138.idiomatic: Gaozu took the lesson, swallowed the advice whole, and ennobled Lou Jing as a Liu.

s0139.literal: Further he turned declaring to Lu Jia: 'For me compose how Qin perished—and how myself obtained.'
s0139.idiomatic: He likewise told Lu Jia: 'Draft for me why Qin fell and why I survived.'

s0140.literal: ' Jia thereupon authored 'New Discourses'-book—narrating former generations success-failure to serve advising caution.
s0140.idiomatic: Lu Jia then wrote New Discourses, laying out successive dynasties' rises and crashes as cautionary mirror.'

s0141.literal: Further Tian Ken proposed one-utterance stratagem—not blood kin offspring none may be sent prince-over Qi—and received thousand-catty gold reward-grant.
s0141.idiomatic: Tian Ken's single blunt warning—that only imperial sons should rule Qi—won him gold measured by the thousand-piece.

s0142.literal: Thus the age lauded Han Ancestor's broad enlightened vast acceptance—whereby succeeded completing imperial achievement.
s0142.idiomatic: Hence posterity praises Gaozu's spacious mind—how else could the Han dynasty have cohered?

s0143.literal: Those who speak nowadays of generations all pronounce Yao-Shun anew reborn—all-under-heaven already Great Tranquility.
s0143.idiomatic: Modern chatter insists Yao and Shun have returned and peace reigns outright.

s0144.literal: Your servant alone holds not-thus—also covertly lodges counsel.
s0144.idiomatic: I alone dissent—and still venture counsel.

s0145.literal: Moreover hundred monarchs dangling institutions, saints worthies spit-forth doctrines—forthcoming affair's luminous mirror lies therein.
s0145.idiomatic: Countless rulers left institutions; sages left maxims—all are mirrors for posterity.

s0146.literal: Mencius states: '[Even] Yao cannot bestow empire on Shun—so Shun possessing empire arose from Heaven gifting.'
s0146.idiomatic: Mencius said: Not even Yao could hand empire to Shun outright—his throne was Heaven's gift.'

s0147.literal: Formerly Shun acted minister—Yao perished—the three-years mourning finished—Shun avoided Yao's son south of southern River—realm's nobles dukes who court-paid, who plead lawsuits, proceeded not unto Yao's son but proceeded unto Shun.
s0147.idiomatic: When Shun was minister and Yao died, after mourning Shun withdrew south of the river; lords bearing tribute and plaintiffs seeking judgments sought Shun rather than Yao's heir.'

s0148.literal: Shun proclaimed 'Heaven;' then he entered Middle Region, trod heavenly-son throne.
s0148.idiomatic: Recognizing Heaven's mandate, Shun returned to the heartland and mounted the throne.'

s0149.literal: If [he] dwelt Yao's palace, pressed Yao's son—[that] is not Heaven's conferral.
s0149.idiomatic: Had he squatted in Yao's halls and bullied Yao's son, that would not be Heaven's gift.'

s0150.literal: ' Long-ago west held non-subject Shu—east held usurping-title Wu—three lords tripod-footed—together styled Son of Heaven.
s0150.idiomatic: Lately Shu in the west withheld allegiance, Wu in the east proclaimed its own reign, and three thrones stood tripod-wise, each daring the title Son of Heaven.'

s0151.literal: Wei Wendi led myriad-chariots' host, received abdication at Mipi-bank—yet himself thought virtue matched Tang-Yu—deemed Han Xiandi equaled archaic Yao—self-deemed equaled present Shun—then pronounced Meng Ke, Sun Qing unversed shan-dai's vicissitudes—thereupon authored shan-dai's text, carved stone hanging caution, promulgated displayed all-under-heaven, transmitted posterity generations—how could it make yet-to-come noble men all clearly grasp heart-convinced its righteousness!
s0151.idiomatic: Yet Cao Pi brought an army of ten thousand chariots to Mipi to take the abdication—then styled himself Yao and Shun reborn, cast Emperor Xian as ancient Yao, himself as modern Shun, dismissed Mencius and Xunzi for missing the point of abdication, carved his own charter in stone, and broadcast it as eternal law—how could that ever persuade future gentlemen?

s0152.literal: Yet Wei Wendi vainly yearned Yao-Shun's names, pushed fresh-convened Wei, wished match Tang-Yu's splendor—overlooked bone-flesh favor-forgot barricade-screen's solidity—ultimately could not make four seas guest-submit, merge-unify imperial transformation—while at that time assembled ministers none remonstrated—was that not excess-fault!
s0152.idiomatic: He only aped the labels of Yao and Shun, forced a brand-new Wei, and imagined rivaling the golden age—while casting aside kinship and crumbling the walls of princely support. The realm never truly bowed, unification never arrived, and not one minister dared object—what a failure!

s0153.literal: Sun Qing states: 'Yao-Shun abdication-shan-rang—this is not so.'
s0153.idiomatic: Xunzi declared: 'The tale of Yao and Shun peacefully yielding the throne is simply wrong.'

s0154.literal: As for all-under-heaven—it is utmost weight—without utmost strength none can bear it;
s0154.idiomatic: The realm is the heaviest burden—only the mightiest can shoulder it.

s0155.literal: utmost vastness—without utmost eloquence none can divide it;
s0155.idiomatic: It is the broadest domain—only the clearest debater can parse it.

s0156.literal: utmost multitude—without utmost luminosity none can survey it.
s0156.idiomatic: It is the teeming mass—only the sharpest eye can oversee it.

s0157.literal: These three utmosts—without sage none can exhaust them.'
s0157.idiomatic: None but a sage can master all three.'

s0158.literal: From this speaking, Sun Qing, Meng Ke each also possessed what they did not adopt.
s0158.idiomatic: So Xunzi and Mencius each declined part of the other's lesson.

s0159.literal: Your Majesty received abdication—east quarter entered west palace—arms' blades gleamed heaven—banners' flags eclipsed sun.
s0159.idiomatic: When you took the throne you marched from the eastern offices into the western palace—blades flashed sky-high, standards blotted out the sun.

s0160.literal: Though responding Heaven obeying men, tokens matching Tang-Yu—yet laws' measures' cuts-additions then also differed not from former Wei Wendi—therefore ought draw on three-utmosts to strengthen coercing it.
s0160.idiomatic: Though you answered Heaven and the people like the ancient model, the legal adjustments differed little from Cao Pi's coup—so you must lean on Xunzi's three 'utmosts' to brace the state.

s0161.literal: Yet now the host of royals possess founding-state's name—yet lack breast-sash girdle-belt's substance.
s0161.idiomatic: Today the kings bear state titles but none hold real border command like a true girdle around the capital.

s0162.literal: Further Shu territory possesses nature's dangerous defiles—this is successive generations' treacherous heroes' object of covetous gaze, fugitives' place of gathering—yet lacks kinsmen posterity son-nephews' guard—how can this be deep pondering far planning, damming seepage preventing buds!
s0162.idiomatic: Shu is a natural fortress every warlord envies and every rebel flees toward—yet no imperial kinsman holds it. Is that prudent foresight or choke-point policy?

s0163.literal: Formerly Han Wendi leaned on already-complete enterprise—six directions shared one wind—all-under-heaven single household.
s0163.idiomatic: Even Han Wendi ruled an empire already knitted into one breeze, one hearth.

s0164.literal: Yet Jia Yi ascended memorial outlining that hour's tendencies—still likened circumstance to clasping flame placing pile-on kindling below—upon it sleeping fire not yet flaming—accordingly deeming-it secure.
s0164.idiomatic: Still Jia Yi warned Wen was cuddling glowing coals piled on firewood while declaring himself safe.

s0165.literal: This speech truly preserved not-forgetting perdition amid peace, tranquility not-forgetting tumult.
s0165.idiomatic: That is candor remembering ruin in security and unrest in calm.

s0166.literal: Yet servant's sincerity-sincere also secretly desires Your Majesty dwell peace ponder peril—speak-not 'loftily lofty above' forever—often reflect facing-deep's duty-not-forget treading ice's injunction.
s0166.idiomatic: I beg you not to presume you sit too high forever—dwell on vertigo beside a cliff and ice underfoot.

s0167.literal: Exhaust-removing Wei-era's harm-laws—pacify-using new governance's great transformation—make myriad regions bliss-bliss joyous—joyfully carry Great Bounty—even insects grasses trees all soak grace-moisture.
s0167.idiomatic: Scrub Wei malpractice, widen your new statutes until every kingdom sings and even bugs and grasses drink your bounty.

s0168.literal: Court recites Tranquility-song's hymns—hill-grove possesses none felling '[Zhan]Tan' fellows—this solidly constitutes all-under-heaven's object of expectancy-gaze.
s0168.idiomatic: Let the halls echo the hymn of orderly rule and the hills harbour no starving woodcutter—that is what the empire watches for.

s0169.literal: Your Majesty from first treading throne platform issued no-taboo edict—installed admonition-remonstrance officials—brilliantly favored distinct outspoken ministers—to clarify loving straight-speech's trust—lest memorializers know straight-speech unemployed—all seal-mouth knot-tongue—auspicious portents moreover how whereby arrive!
s0169.idiomatic: From your very accession you invited blunt counsel and prized outspoken aides—yet if plain advice is quietly shelved tongues knot shut and auspicious omens never arrive anyway!

s0170.literal: Your servant lacks Lu-born's talents—not located counsel-inquiry precinct—generally hear lord sage minister straight—duty resides having offence lacking concealment.
s0170.idiomatic: I am no Lu Jia—you did not summon me—but the maxim holds: under a sage king ministers must speak straight even when it hurts.

s0171.literal: Your servant not-only remote-estranged, un-trusted yet speaking—dares traverse-discuss anterior generations lofty-name rulers and perdition-collapsed rulers' rise-fall causal-chains—further broadly presents raising-worthies's roadways—broad-opening nursing-elderlies' systems—elevate surely-trusted way—again arrays debaters's difficulties—all five affairs to memorialize-report.
s0171.idiomatic: Though I am insignificant and unheard, I will survey famous rises and rotten falls, map paths for talent, widen care for elders, reaffirm sincerity, rehearse objections—five headings in all.

s0172.literal: That which your servant utters—all straight-announce ancient-present already-practiced precedents—not new-tone heterodox doctrines.
s0172.idiomatic: Nothing here is novelty—only what history already tried.

s0173.literal: Diction righteousness truly shallow—not worth picking accepting.
s0173.idiomatic: My phrasing stays thin—barely worthy of inclusion.

s0174.literal: Yet servant's private heart sincerely holds feasible rousing awaken forgotten-lapses.
s0174.idiomatic: Yet I hope scraps of it jog what memory forgets.

s0175.literal: Willing Your Majesty inspect servant ignorant loyalty—pity servant mad straight—cause-not all-under-heaven deem speech-makers-warning.
s0175.idiomatic: Please read this dull loyalty kindly so the world learns blunt words are safe.

s0176.literal: Ill-pain aggravated severe—draw back pondering mulberry-fields' ode—ponder fox-death righteousness—accordingly seize extended resting—return approaching grave-mounds.
s0176.idiomatic: Pain worsened; I heed the hymn of homecomings and the maxim that foxes prefer their birthplace—long leave it is so I might die near ancestral tombs.

s0177.literal: Glancing imperial-palaces—heart bound sagely-pole—not overcome cinnabar candidness—dispatch heir Ying ascend memorial speech.
s0177.idiomatic: My eyes cling to palace gates though my spine fails—so I risk honesty through my son Ying's pen.

s0178.literal: First item declares: Your servant hears good possessing manifest rules—indelibly fixed in scriptures-classics;
s0178.idiomatic: First: deeds of good lie spelled out in the canon.

s0179.literal: evil possessing penalties—warnings reside criminal codices.
s0179.idiomatic: Wrongs live under the lash of written law.

s0180.literal: Above from remote antiquity, below descending to Qin Han—those luminous kings hegemons and extinguished-country dim rulers—for these one can obtain appellations;
s0180.idiomatic: From farthest antiquity through Qin and Han you can tally bright rulers, dark losers, conquerors gone under.

s0181.literal: stretching unto loyal arduous worthy chancellors and fawning crafty evil ministers—for these likewise one can articulate.
s0181.idiomatic: You can also name steadfast ministers beside conniving villains.

s0182.literal: Therefore court possessing outspoken blunt exhaust-regulation ministers—never not flourished;
s0182.idiomatic: Courts stocked with quarrelsome straight men always flourished.

s0183.literal: employing yielding flattery yes-yes gents—never not perished.
s0183.idiomatic: Courts manned by yes-men vanished without exception.

s0184.literal: Those possessing states altogether wish seek loyalty to assist self—elevate worthy to aid self;
s0184.idiomatic: Every sovereign wants loyalty to prop him up and genius to sharpen him.

s0185.literal: yet perdition-collapsed ruined-house ones succeed one-after-another—altogether stemming from employing losing its proper men.
s0185.idiomatic: Yet ruin follows ruin because the wrong faces fill the mats.

s0186.literal: What is termed worthy—is not worthy; termed loyal—not loyal.
s0186.idiomatic: They call allies worthy who are worthless, loyal who are thieves.

s0187.literal: Your servant respectfully recounts predecessors' employing worthies causal rise, employing unworthies causal fall.
s0187.idiomatic: I recount how predecessors rose on talent and sank on villains.

s0188.literal: Yao's late years—the four fierce ones stationed court yet departed not—the eight perfected ones lodged home yet summoned not—nevertheless effected heaven-flat earth tranquillity—four Gates augustly majestic—whose achievement solidly lodged in Chonghua's functioning minister.
s0188.idiomatic: Late Yao let four beasts squat in council while ignoring the Eight Paragons, yet harmony held—credit belongs to Shun as minister.

s0189.literal: Jie of Xia was driven out at Mingtiao—Xin of Shang had his severed head displayed at Muye—these jointly myriad-chariot's lords—yet state extinguished body seized—stemming from inability consecrate-assign worthy minister—employing woman's speech—dissolute riot lacking way license-will drowned feast—composed wan-wan melodies—drawn-out night's drinking—thereupon ascending lees mound—overlooking wine pool—surveying cattle guzzling—gazing carnal forest—Guan Longpang loyal yet suffered harm—Bi Gan remonstrating yet torso cleaved—all-under-heaven's cause for returning malignance.
s0189.idiomatic: Jie of Xia ended in defeat at Mingtiao; Zhou of Shang hung as a trophy at Muye—each commanded ten thousand chariots yet lost throne and life for heeding women rather than ministers, wallowing in debauch: mounds of mash, pools of wine, oxen drinking like men, groves of roasting meat—until loyal Guan Longpang died for speaking truth and blunt Bi Gan lost his heart—all under Heaven turned their hatred toward them.

s0190.literal: Tai Jia riot-cruel—overturned Tang's statutes—thereupon Yi Yin expelled him to the Tong Palace—and could reform regret turn good—three years afterward returned toward Bo-capital.
s0190.idiomatic: Tai Jia trampled Tang's ordinances, so Yi Yin confined him in the Tong Palace until he repented; three years later he restored him to Bo, the royal seat.

s0191.literal: Already once expelled afterward again returned—Yin-way declined-yet anew prospered—all nobles together submitted—designation styled Grand Ancestor—solidly leaned on A-heng Yi Yin's exhaust-loyalty.
s0191.idiomatic: Once restored, the Shang line rallied from decline and every lord submitted; he earned the temple epithet Taizong—thanks wholly to Yi Yin's single-minded devotion.

s0192.literal: Zhou house already declined—nobles feudatories together quarreled—heaven king frail weakened—government thereupon hillside-slipped tardy-decayed.
s0192.idiomatic: When Zhou sank, feudatories warred together, kings grew feeble and policy slid downhill.

s0193.literal: Qi Huan Gong—dissolute turbulent ruler ear;
s0193.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi lived as a voluptuary.

s0194.literal: yet whereby could nine alliances one rectification merits—hold honouring Zhou's fame—truthfully steward-yi Zhong's power.
s0194.idiomatic: Yet he knit nine alliances and forced order on the empire—chiefly because of Guan Zhong.

s0195.literal: Reaching unto his demise—worm-maggots oozed out gate—could it lack appointing Shu Diao fault!
s0195.idiomatic: Dead, his corpse maggotted into the hallway—surely Shu Diao's fault.

s0196.literal: Moreover one Huan Gong torso—obtained Guan Zhong—his feats like-so;
s0196.idiomatic: The same man's body—with Guan Zhong he soared.

s0198.literal: As for glory-shame perdurance-extinction—in truth settles on whom entrusted—might one not scrutinize attentively!
s0198.idiomatic: Glory or ruin hinges on ministers chosen—inspect that choice fiercely.

s0199.literal: Qin's root descended Boyi's posteriors—minute minute tiny walled-place—until Qin Zhong first enlarged—having chariot-horse ritual-music attendant-guards' beauties therein.
s0199.idiomatic: Qin traced back to Boyi—once a petty stockade—until Zhong enlarged it toward chariotry and court music.

s0200.literal: From Duke Mu stretching unto First Emperor—all could devote heart awaiting worthies—far seek uncommon gentlemen—summon You Yu amidst western Rong—deliver Five Black Rams unto Wan market—capture Pi Leopard within Jin outskirts—welcome Jian Shu at Zong village.
s0200.idiomatic: From Duke Mu onward every ruler hunted talent—You Yu from the west, five rams swapped in Nanyang, Pi Leopard torn from Jin, Jian Shu coaxed down from Zong village.
